q: During his inspection of a station, the Travelling Inspector of Accounts, among other things:

options.A: Sanctions the refunds of fares claimed at the station
options.B: Fixes the earnings targets of the station
options.C: Verifies the cash balance of the station with the balance shown in the station accounts and reports any discrepancy
options.D: Prepares the salary bills of the station staff

e: During station inspection, the Travelling Inspector of Accounts verifies the station's cash balance against the balance shown in the station accounts and reports any discrepancy noticed.

q: The Traffic Accounts Office of a zonal railway functions under the overall control of the:

options.A: General Manager
options.B: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer (FA & CAO) of the railway
options.C: Divisional Railway Manager
options.D: Railway Board directly

e: The Traffic Accounts Office of a zonal railway functions under the overall control of the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer (FA and CAO) of that railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Through goods traffic is exchanged with the neighbouring foreign railways, such as those of Bangladesh and Nepal, at nominated interchange points.
2. The earnings of such international traffic are apportioned and settled between the railway administrations concerned on agreed principles.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: through goods traffic is exchanged with neighbouring foreign railways such as Bangladesh and Nepal at nominated interchange points, and the earnings are apportioned and settled between the administrations on agreed principles.

q: For compiling passenger statistics, the journeys performed on season tickets are accounted for by:

options.A: Counting the season tickets sold as one journey each
options.B: Estimating the number of journeys on a prescribed standard basis, as the actual journeys made by each holder are not recorded
options.C: Excluding season ticket holders from the passenger statistics altogether
options.D: Counting only the journeys on which the tickets are physically checked

e: Since the actual journeys made on a season ticket are not recorded, passenger statistics estimate the number of journeys on a prescribed standard basis for each season ticket sold.

q: 'Earnings per route kilometre' of a railway is computed as:

options.A: Goods earnings divided by goods train kilometres
options.B: Net revenue divided by the capital-at-charge
options.C: Passenger earnings divided by passenger kilometres
options.D: Gross traffic earnings divided by the route kilometres open for traffic

e: Earnings per route kilometre = gross traffic earnings divided by the route kilometres open for traffic; it measures the earning intensity of the network.

q: 'Passengers carried' on a railway comprise:

options.A: Only the passengers who alight at its stations
options.B: Originating passengers plus the passengers received from other railways
options.C: Only the passengers booked at its own stations in cash
options.D: The passengers who travel by reserved coaches only

e: Passengers carried by a railway comprise its originating passengers plus the passengers received from other railways, so that all passengers it actually conveys are counted.

q: An undercharge in freight detected at the destination station on a 'to-pay' consignment is:

options.A: Recovered from the consignee before delivery of the goods
options.B: Written off by the destination station
options.C: Recovered from the forwarding station staff
options.D: Adjusted against the sundry earnings of the station

e: An undercharge detected at destination on a 'to-pay' consignment is recovered from the consignee before delivery of the goods, since freight on a to-pay consignment is collected at destination.

q: The superfast charge levied on passengers travelling by superfast trains forms part of:

options.A: Sundry other earnings
options.B: Coaching earnings
options.C: Goods earnings
options.D: Miscellaneous receipts of the division

e: The superfast charge is a component of the passenger fare structure for superfast trains and therefore forms part of coaching earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The wharfage and demurrage returns rendered by stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office to ensure that the charges have been correctly levied and fully brought to account.
2. This check also covers that no waiver or remission of such charges has been allowed except under the orders of the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: the Traffic Accounts Office checks stations' wharfage and demurrage returns to ensure the charges are correctly levied and fully brought to account, and that no waiver or remission was allowed except under the competent authority's orders.

q: The free allowance of luggage admissible to a passenger travelling by rail:

options.A: Is the same for all classes of travel
options.B: Depends upon the class in which the passenger travels
options.C: Depends only on the distance of the journey
options.D: Depends only on the type of train by which he travels

e: The free luggage allowance varies with the class of travel: higher classes carry a larger free allowance, so it is not uniform for all passengers.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Statement 6A shows the approximate gross earnings of a railway and is compiled for each period of ten days.
2. Statement 7A shows the gross earnings of a railway for the month as finally brought to account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: Statement 6A shows the approximate gross earnings compiled for each period of ten days, while Statement 7A shows the gross earnings for the month as finally brought to account after check.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Traffic Book:
1. Part A of the Traffic Book deals with through traffic, the earnings of which are to be apportioned among the railways concerned.
2. Part B of the Traffic Book deals with local traffic, the earnings of which are retained wholly by the home railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: Part A of the Traffic Book deals with through traffic whose earnings are apportioned among the railways concerned, and Part B deals with local traffic whose earnings the home railway retains wholly.

q: A Railway Receipt is a document of title to the goods, which means that:

options.A: It can never be transferred to another person
options.B: The right to take delivery of the goods can be transferred by endorsement and delivery of the Railway Receipt
options.C: It is valid only in favour of the consignor named on it
options.D: It serves only as a cash receipt for the freight paid

e: As a document of title, the Railway Receipt represents the goods; the right to take delivery can be transferred to another person by endorsement and delivery of the Receipt.

q: The document executed by the consignor at the time of booking goods, containing the description, weight and other particulars of the consignment and the consignor's declaration, is known as the:

options.A: Forwarding Note
options.B: Parcel Way Bill
options.C: Delivery Book
options.D: Gate Pass

e: The Forwarding Note is the document executed by the consignor at booking, containing the description, weight and other particulars of the consignment along with the consignor's declaration.

q: Under the Railways Act, the railway administration may detain a consignment and exercise a lien on it until:

options.A: The end of the financial year
options.B: The freight and all other charges due in respect of the consignment are paid
options.C: The consignee obtains an order of the Claims Tribunal
options.D: Thirty days have elapsed after its arrival at destination

e: Under the Railways Act, the railway administration may detain a consignment and exercise a lien on it until the freight and all other charges due in respect of it are paid.

q: Where the consignor does not declare the value of the consignment and does not pay the percentage charge, the position regarding the Railways' liability for loss of or damage to the goods is that:

options.A: The Railways bear unlimited liability as in the case of declared-value consignments
options.B: The monetary liability of the Railways is limited as prescribed under the Railways Act
options.C: The Railways bear no liability at all
options.D: The liability is borne personally by the forwarding station staff

e: If the consignor does not declare the value and pay the percentage charge, the Railways' monetary liability for loss or damage is limited to the extent prescribed under the Railways Act.

q: Claims for compensation for death of, or injury to, passengers in a train accident or an untoward incident are decided by the:

options.A: Divisional Railway Manager
options.B: Railway Board
options.C: District Consumer Commission only
options.D: Railway Claims Tribunal

e: Claims for compensation for death of or injury to passengers in a train accident or an untoward incident are adjudicated by the Railway Claims Tribunal.

q: The excess charge leviable under the Railways Act from a person found travelling without a proper ticket is payable:

options.A: In addition to the ordinary fare due for the distance travelled
options.B: In lieu of the ordinary fare for the distance travelled
options.C: Only where the person is also found carrying excess luggage
options.D: Only by season ticket holders

e: The excess charge for travelling without a proper ticket is levied in addition to the ordinary fare due for the distance travelled; it does not replace the fare.

q: Which of the following is a recognised circumstance in which waiver of demurrage accrued at a station may be considered by the competent authority?

options.A: The consignee is a regular customer of the Railways
options.B: Wagons were placed in a bunch, in excess of the party's requirements, so that unloading within the free time was not practicable
options.C: The goods carried are of high value
options.D: The station is a busy terminal station

e: Demurrage waiver may be considered where wagons were placed in a bunch, in excess of the party's requirements, making unloading within the free time impracticable; mere regular custom or high value of goods is no ground.

q: On cancellation of a confirmed Tatkal ticket by the passenger, the refund position is that:

options.A: Full fare is refunded without any deduction
options.B: Fifty per cent of the fare is refunded
options.C: Only the reservation charge is refunded
options.D: No refund is admissible, except in the circumstances specified in the refund rules such as cancellation of the train

e: No refund is admissible on cancellation of a confirmed Tatkal ticket by the passenger, except in the circumstances specified in the refund rules, such as cancellation of the train itself.

q: Where a passenger reports the loss of a confirmed reserved ticket before preparation of the chart, a duplicate ticket may be issued:

options.A: Free of charge in all cases
options.B: Only after the journey is completed
options.C: On recovery of the prescribed charges, subject to the conditions laid down in the Coaching Tariff
options.D: Only at the destination station

e: For a lost confirmed reserved ticket reported before preparation of the chart, a duplicate ticket may be issued on recovery of the prescribed charges, subject to the conditions in the Coaching Tariff.

q: Freight on bulk commodities loaded in open wagons, such as coal and ores, is generally charged on the basis of:

options.A: The carrying capacity of the wagon used
options.B: The volume of the wagon
options.C: A flat rate per wagon, irrespective of the wagon used
options.D: The value of the commodity

e: Freight on bulk commodities like coal and ores loaded in open wagons is generally charged on the carrying capacity of the wagon used, rather than on the actual weight loaded.

q: 'Wagonload' class rates in goods traffic are applicable where:

options.A: A full rake load of traffic is offered for booking
options.B: Traffic is offered in wagon loads which do not make up a full rake load
options.C: Traffic is carried in the brake vans of passenger trains
options.D: The consignment weighs less than the prescribed minimum for 'smalls'

e: Wagonload class rates apply where traffic is offered in wagon loads that do not make up a full rake (train) load; full rake loads attract trainload rates instead.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where the FOIS is not available at a station due to failure of the system, goods booking is carried out manually under the prescribed contingency arrangements.
2. The particulars of consignments booked manually during such failure are fed into the system when it is restored, so that the traffic is duly accounted for.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: if FOIS fails at a station, goods booking is done manually under the prescribed contingency arrangements, and the particulars of such bookings are fed into the system on its restoration so the traffic is duly accounted for.

q: Hire charges for wagons of one railway used by another railway are settled between the railways concerned primarily on the basis of:

options.A: The earnings of the user railway
options.B: The number of wagons built by each railway
options.C: The capital-at-charge of the owner railway
options.D: The interchange records of wagons handed over and received between the railways

e: Hire charges for wagons of one railway used by another are settled primarily on the basis of the interchange records of wagons handed over and received between the railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The goods wagons of the zonal railways form a common pool and are freely interchanged among the railways for loading.
2. A zonal railway may load only the wagons owned by it and must return other railways' wagons empty immediately on receipt.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: wagons of the zonal railways form a common pool and are freely interchanged for loading. Statement 2 is false: a railway may load other railways' wagons and need not return them empty immediately.

q: During the inspection of a station, the Travelling Inspector of Accounts also verifies:

options.A: The personal cash of the booking clerks
options.B: The catering arrangements at the station
options.C: The punctuality of trains at the station
options.D: The physical stock of tickets and money-value books with the ticket stock register of the station

e: During inspection, the Travelling Inspector of Accounts also verifies the physical stock of tickets and money-value books against the station's ticket stock register.

q: Amounts debited to a station which are found to be irrecoverable can be written off only:

options.A: By the Station Master at the end of the month
options.B: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his inspection
options.C: Under the sanction of the competent authority, with the concurrence of the Finance/Accounts branch
options.D: By adjustment against the earnings of the following month

e: Amounts debited to a station that are found irrecoverable can be written off only under the sanction of the competent authority, with the concurrence of the Finance/Accounts branch.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Reservation charges recovered from passengers form part of the passenger (coaching) earnings of the Railways.
2. The cancellation charges retained by the Railways on cancellation of tickets also form part of the coaching earnings.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: reservation charges recovered from passengers and the cancellation charges retained on cancelled tickets both form part of the passenger (coaching) earnings of the Railways.

q: The convenience fee (service charge) levied by IRCTC on passengers booking e-tickets is:

options.A: An earning of the Railways, remitted by IRCTC every month
options.B: Retained by IRCTC and does not form part of the earnings of the Railways
options.C: Shared equally between IRCTC and the Railways
options.D: Credited to the Traffic Suspense of the Railways

e: The convenience fee on e-tickets is IRCTC's own service charge; it is retained by IRCTC and does not form part of the earnings of the Railways.

q: Tatkal premium charges collected from passengers form part of:

options.A: Sundry other earnings
options.B: Passenger (coaching) earnings
options.C: Goods earnings
options.D: Miscellaneous receipts of the division

e: Tatkal premium charges are a component of the passenger fare collected for tatkal bookings and therefore form part of passenger (coaching) earnings.

q: Which of the following represents a social service obligation borne by the Railways?

options.A: Operation of commercially viable long-distance trains
options.B: Concessions in passenger fares and losses on uneconomic branch lines
options.C: Payment of dividend to General Revenues
options.D: Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: Social service obligations are the losses the Railways bear for social reasons, principally concessions in passenger fares and the operation of uneconomic branch lines retained for public need.

q: 'Earnings per passenger' of a railway are computed as:

options.A: Passenger earnings divided by the number of passengers carried
options.B: Passenger earnings divided by passenger kilometres
options.C: Coaching earnings divided by train kilometres
options.D: Passenger kilometres divided by the number of passengers

e: Earnings per passenger = passenger earnings divided by the number of passengers carried; it gives the average fare realised per passenger conveyed.

q: 'Earnings per tonne carried' in goods traffic are computed as:

options.A: Goods earnings divided by the total tonnes carried
options.B: Goods earnings divided by Net Tonne Kilometres
options.C: Goods earnings divided by tonnes originating only
options.D: Tonnes carried divided by the number of wagons loaded

e: Earnings per tonne carried = goods earnings divided by the total tonnes carried; it is based on total tonnes, not on Net Tonne Kilometres or originating tonnes alone.

q: The average number of coaches (vehicles) per passenger train is computed as:

options.A: Vehicle kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres
options.B: Passenger kilometres divided by train kilometres
options.C: Seat kilometres divided by vehicle kilometres
options.D: Train kilometres divided by route kilometres

e: Average coaches per passenger train = vehicle kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres; dividing the total coach-distance run by the train-distance run gives the average formation length.

q: The average speed of passenger trains is computed as:

options.A: Route kilometres divided by the number of trains
options.B: Passenger kilometres divided by passenger train hours
options.C: Vehicle kilometres divided by vehicle days
options.D: Passenger train kilometres divided by the corresponding train hours

e: Average speed of passenger trains = passenger train kilometres divided by the corresponding train hours, i.e., the distance run per hour of train running time.

q: 'Passenger kilometres per vehicle day' is an index which measures:

options.A: The speed of coaching services
options.B: The traffic output obtained from coaching vehicles, i.e. their utilisation in terms of passenger traffic performed
options.C: The earnings of coaching services per day
options.D: The punctuality of passenger trains

e: Passenger kilometres per vehicle day measures the traffic output obtained from coaching vehicles, showing how productively each vehicle is utilised in performing passenger traffic per day.

q: In traffic costing, 'terminal cost' means:

options.A: The costs incurred at the originating and destination terminals in handling the traffic, such as loading, unloading and documentation
options.B: The cost of constructing terminal stations
options.C: The cost of hauling traffic between the terminals
options.D: The interest on capital invested in terminal facilities

e: In traffic costing, terminal cost means the costs incurred at the originating and destination terminals in handling the traffic, such as loading, unloading and documentation, as distinct from line-haul cost.

q: Inland Container Depots (ICDs) operated by CONCOR are:

options.A: Ports located on the sea coast
options.B: Dry ports where export/import containers are handled and customs formalities are completed away from the seaports
options.C: Depots for storing railway stores
options.D: Terminals meant exclusively for parcel traffic

e: Inland Container Depots are dry ports operated by CONCOR where export and import containers are handled and customs formalities are completed inland, away from the seaports.

q: Container traffic on the Railways is measured in 'TEUs', which stands for:

options.A: Transport Equipment Units
options.B: Twenty-foot Equivalent Units
options.C: Terminal Evacuation Units
options.D: Total Earnings Units

e: TEU stands for Twenty-foot Equivalent Units, the standard unit for measuring container traffic, one TEU being equivalent to one twenty-foot container.

q: Haulage charges received from CONCOR for the movement of container trains over the railway network form part of:

options.A: Sundry other earnings
options.B: Coaching earnings
options.C: Capital receipts
options.D: Goods earnings

e: Haulage charges received from CONCOR for moving container trains over the railway network are a traffic receipt from goods services and form part of goods earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Parties may book special trains or reserved coaches on payment of charges at the Full Tariff Rate (FTR).
2. The charges so recovered by the Railways form part of the coaching earnings.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: special trains or reserved coaches can be booked on payment of charges at the Full Tariff Rate (FTR), and the charges so recovered form part of coaching earnings.

q: In connection with parcel traffic, the abbreviation PMS stands for:

options.A: Parcel Movement Section
options.B: Passenger Mail Service
options.C: Parcel Marketing Scheme
options.D: Parcel Management System

e: PMS stands for Parcel Management System, the computerised system for booking, carriage and delivery of parcel traffic.

q: Hand Held Terminals (HHTs) are used by the ticket checking staff on trains for:

options.A: Issuing unreserved tickets at stations
options.B: Printing the reservation charts at the starting station
options.C: Checking the tickets of passengers and allotting vacant berths on the train, the data being synchronised with the reservation system
options.D: Collecting freight from goods customers

e: Hand Held Terminals are used by ticket checking staff on trains to check passengers' tickets and allot vacant berths, the data being synchronised with the central reservation system.

q: Under the Freight Operations Information System, the Railway Receipt for a consignment is:

options.A: Generated electronically by the system on capture of the booking particulars
options.B: Written by hand by the goods clerk in all cases
options.C: Issued by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: Prepared by the consignor himself

e: Under the Freight Operations Information System, the Railway Receipt is generated electronically by the system once the booking particulars of the consignment are captured.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Earnings of the Railways are accounted on the accrual basis, so that 'to-pay' freight on goods delivered but remaining unpaid at the close of the year is included in the earnings of that year.
2. Such unpaid amounts remain held under Traffic Suspense till they are realised or adjusted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: railway earnings are accounted on the accrual basis, so unpaid 'to-pay' freight on goods delivered by the year-end is included in that year's earnings, and such amounts remain under Traffic Suspense till realised or adjusted.

q: Demurrage and wharfage charges due on a consignment are required to be paid:

options.A: Within thirty days of delivery of the goods
options.B: At the end of the financial year
options.C: Only if the amount exceeds the freight paid
options.D: Before the goods are delivered or removed from the station premises

e: Demurrage and wharfage charges due on a consignment must be paid before the goods are delivered or removed from the station premises.

q: 'Train kilometres per route kilometre' on a section indicates:

options.A: The density or intensity of the train services operated on the section
options.B: The average speed of trains on the section
options.C: The earnings of the section
options.D: The number of stations on the section

e: Train kilometres per route kilometre shows the density, or intensity, of the train services operated on a section - how much train movement each route kilometre carries.

q: 'Earnings per coaching train kilometre' are computed as:

options.A: Passenger earnings divided by passenger kilometres
options.B: Coaching earnings divided by the number of coaches
options.C: Passenger kilometres divided by coaching train kilometres
options.D: Coaching earnings divided by coaching train kilometres

e: Earnings per coaching train kilometre = coaching earnings divided by coaching train kilometres; it measures the average coaching realisation for each kilometre run by a coaching train.

q: For statistical purposes, the wagon fleet and wagon-day statistics of Indian Railways are expressed in terms of:

options.A: Eight-wheeler units
options.B: Bogie units
options.C: Four-wheeler units
options.D: Rake units

e: For statistical purposes, the wagon fleet and wagon-day statistics of Indian Railways are expressed in terms of four-wheeler units, bogie wagons being converted into equivalent four-wheeler units.

q: Demurrage at a goods terminal is computed with reference to:

options.A: The time of placement of the wagons for loading or unloading and the time of their release, as recorded in the terminal records/system
options.B: The date of booking of the consignment
options.C: The date of preparation of the Railway Receipt
options.D: The date of arrival of the train at the nearest junction

e: Demurrage at a goods terminal is computed with reference to the time the wagons are placed for loading or unloading and the time they are released, as recorded in the terminal records or system.

q: A consignee who doubts the weight of a consignment may obtain its re-weighment at the destination station:

options.A: Free of charge in all cases
options.B: On payment of the prescribed weighment charges
options.C: Only through an order of the Claims Tribunal
options.D: Only at the forwarding station

e: A consignee doubting the weight of a consignment may get it re-weighed at the destination station on payment of the prescribed weighment charges; re-weighment is not free.

q: A waitlisted e-ticket which does not get confirmed on preparation of the reservation chart is:

options.A: Automatically cancelled and the fare refunded to the passenger's account
options.B: Carried forward to the next day's chart
options.C: Converted into an unreserved ticket
options.D: Kept valid for travel in the unreserved coach

e: A waitlisted e-ticket that remains unconfirmed on preparation of the reservation chart is automatically cancelled and the fare is refunded to the passenger's account.

q: Parcel traffic on Indian Railways is generally carried:

options.A: Only by goods trains
options.B: Only by road vehicles hired by the Railways
options.C: By passenger-carrying trains, in brake/luggage vans and parcel vans attached to them
options.D: Only by special parcel trains and by no other train

e: Parcel traffic is generally carried by passenger-carrying trains, in the brake/luggage vans (SLR) and parcel vans attached to them, so that it moves with passenger-train speed.

q: Amounts debited to a station on account of errors or deficiencies in its accounts are ultimately:

options.A: Borne by the Railways as a normal loss in all cases
options.B: Adjusted against the sundry earnings of the station
options.C: Recovered from the passengers and merchants concerned
options.D: Recoverable from the members of the station staff found responsible for the error or deficiency

e: Amounts debited to a station for errors or deficiencies in its accounts are recoverable from the members of the station staff found responsible for the error or deficiency.

q: 'Light engine kilometres' in railway statistics mean:

options.A: Engine kilometres run by shunting engines in yards
options.B: Engine kilometres run by a locomotive without hauling any train or load
options.C: Engine kilometres run by electric locomotives only
options.D: Engine kilometres run on trial trips after repairs

e: Light engine kilometres are the engine kilometres run by a locomotive without hauling any train or load, for example when running to or from a shed or to take up a duty.

q: An 'engine day' in railway statistics represents:

options.A: One engine under repair for a period of 24 hours
options.B: One engine worked on a train during a calendar day
options.C: The day on which an engine is taken for periodical overhaul
options.D: One locomotive on line (available) for a period of 24 hours

e: An engine day represents one locomotive on line, that is available, for a period of 24 hours; engine-day totals are the base for locomotive utilisation indices.

q: The 'total track kilometres' of a railway, as distinct from route kilometres, include:

options.A: Only the main running lines open for traffic
options.B: Only the lines open for passenger traffic
options.C: Running lines together with sidings, yard lines and other tracks, each line being counted separately
options.D: The length of electrified lines only

e: Total track kilometres include the running lines together with sidings, yard lines and other tracks, each line being counted separately, unlike route kilometres, which measure the route length only once.

q: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989 deals with:

options.A: Claims for compensation for loss of goods
options.B: Levy of wharfage and demurrage
options.C: Carriage of dangerous goods
options.D: Fraudulently travelling or attempting to travel without a proper pass or ticket

e: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989 deals with fraudulently travelling or attempting to travel without a proper pass or ticket, and prescribes the punishment for it.

q: Under Section 142 of the Railways Act, 1989:

options.A: Transfer of a ticket or of reserved accommodation by a person other than an authorised railway servant or agent is prohibited and punishable
options.B: Claims for refund of overcharges must be filed within six months
options.C: Passenger fares are fixed by notification in the Gazette
options.D: Demurrage is levied after the expiry of free time

e: Section 142 of the Railways Act, 1989 prohibits the transfer of a ticket or of reserved accommodation by any person other than an authorised railway servant or agent, and makes such transfer punishable.

q: The rules governing the booking and carriage of explosives and other dangerous goods on the Railways are contained in the:

options.A: Coaching Tariff
options.B: Red Tariff
options.C: Works Manual
options.D: Establishment Code

e: The rules for booking and carriage of explosives and other dangerous goods are contained in the Red Tariff, the tariff publication dealing with such traffic.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Goods can be booked 'through' to a destination across a break-of-gauge point under a single Railway Receipt.
2. The transhipment of such goods at the break-of-gauge point is arranged by the Railways as part of the through carriage.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: goods can be booked through to a destination across a break-of-gauge point under a single Railway Receipt, and the transhipment at the break-of-gauge point is arranged by the Railways as part of the through carriage.

q: A consignment which is carried beyond its destination station by mistake is said to be 'overcarried'. Such a consignment is:

options.A: Auctioned at the station where the mistake is detected
options.B: Returned to the consignor at his cost
options.C: Charged freight afresh for the entire journey
options.D: Forwarded to the correct destination at the cost of the Railways, without recovery of extra freight from the party

e: An overcarried consignment, taken beyond its destination by mistake, is forwarded to the correct destination at the cost of the Railways, without recovery of extra freight from the party.

q: 'Rebooking' of a consignment means:

options.A: Booking the consignment afresh from the destination station to another station after it has arrived at the original destination
options.B: Change of the destination while the consignment is still in transit
options.C: Re-weighment of the consignment at the destination
options.D: Issue of a duplicate Railway Receipt

e: Rebooking means booking the consignment afresh from the destination station to another station after it has arrived at the original destination; a change of destination in transit is diversion, not rebooking.

q: Where the packing of a consignment offered for booking is found to be defective, the fact is recorded on the Forwarding Note/Railway Receipt mainly in order to:

options.A: Levy demurrage in advance on the consignment
options.B: Safeguard the Railways against claims for damage attributable to the defective packing
options.C: Raise the freight class of the commodity
options.D: Refuse the consignment outright in all cases

e: Defective packing found at booking is recorded on the Forwarding Note and Railway Receipt mainly to safeguard the Railways against claims for damage that is attributable to the defective packing.

q: In a Station Balance Sheet, the closing outstanding balance of the month is arrived at as:

options.A: The earnings of the month minus the cash held at the station
options.B: The total earnings of the year divided by twelve
options.C: The opening balance, plus the earnings and other debits of the month, minus the remittances and other credits of the month
options.D: The cash remitted to the bank during the month

e: In a Station Balance Sheet, the closing outstanding is the opening balance plus the earnings and other debits of the month, minus the remittances and other credits of the month.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Accounts Office Balance Sheet is compiled independently in the Traffic Accounts Office from its own books and records.
2. The Accounts Office Balance Sheet is merely a copy of the Station Balance Sheet rendered by the station.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: the Accounts Office Balance Sheet is compiled independently in the Traffic Accounts Office from its own books and records. Statement 2 is false: it is not a mere copy of the Station Balance Sheet.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Statutory audit of station accounts is exercised by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts.
2. Statutory audit of railway accounts, including station accounts, is exercised by the Railway Audit organisation working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: the Travelling Inspector of Accounts conducts internal inspection, not statutory audit. Statement 2 is true: statutory audit of railway accounts, including station accounts, is exercised by the Railway Audit organisation under the CAG.

q: Parcel Way Bills rendered by stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office primarily to ensure that:

options.A: The parcels were delivered on the day of arrival
options.B: The parcel vans were utilised to their full capacity
options.C: The parcels were carried only by Rajdhani trains
options.D: The parcel charges have been correctly levied in accordance with the scales in force and duly brought to account

e: Parcel Way Bills rendered by stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office mainly to ensure that the parcel charges have been correctly levied in accordance with the scales in force and duly brought to account.

q: The goods invoices rendered by forwarding stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office with a view to verifying, among other things:

options.A: The correctness of the classification, chargeable weight and freight charged on the consignments
options.B: The handwriting of the goods clerks
options.C: The punctuality of goods trains
options.D: The physical condition of the goods sheds

e: Goods invoices are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office to verify, among other things, the correctness of the classification, the chargeable weight and the freight charged on the consignments.

q: 'Handling bills' rendered by stations relate to:

options.A: Bills for the pay and allowances of goods shed staff
options.B: Payments claimed by contractors engaged for handling, loading and unloading of goods and parcels at stations
options.C: Bills for the printing of goods invoices
options.D: Claims of merchants for damaged goods

e: Handling bills are the payments claimed by contractors engaged for handling, loading and unloading of goods and parcels at stations, rendered by the stations for payment.

q: The apportionment of earnings of through traffic among the zonal railways has the effect of:

options.A: Increasing the total earnings of Indian Railways
options.B: Reducing the total earnings of Indian Railways
options.C: Merely distributing the through earnings among the railways concerned, without altering the total earnings of Indian Railways as a whole
options.D: Transferring the entire earnings to the Railway Board

e: Apportionment merely distributes the earnings of through traffic among the railways concerned according to their shares; the total earnings of Indian Railways as a whole remain unchanged.

q: The apportionment of earnings of through goods traffic among the railways is worked out primarily on the basis of:

options.A: The number of stations on each railway
options.B: The capital-at-charge of each railway
options.C: The staff strength of each railway
options.D: The abstracts of invoices/earnings exchanged between the railways concerned

e: Apportionment of through goods earnings is worked out primarily from the abstracts of invoices and earnings exchanged between the railways concerned, which show the traffic each railway carried and its share.

q: Passenger fares and freight rates on Indian Railways are fixed by:

options.A: The Railway Board (Ministry of Railways)
options.B: The Station Master at each station
options.C: The Finance Commission
options.D: The respective State Governments

e: Passenger fares and freight rates on Indian Railways are fixed by the Railway Board (Ministry of Railways); neither stations nor State Governments have this power.

q: 'Smalls' traffic (less than wagonload consignments) is charged for carriage:

options.A: At trainload rates
options.B: At a scale of rates which is higher per unit of weight than the wagonload scale, in view of the higher cost of handling such traffic
options.C: Free of charge up to the prescribed minimum weight
options.D: At parcel rates in all cases

e: 'Smalls' (less than wagonload) traffic is charged at a scale of rates higher per unit of weight than the wagonload scale, because small consignments cost more to handle, sort and carry.

q: Trainload (rake-load) class rates, as compared with wagonload class rates for the same commodity and distance, are generally:

options.A: Higher per tonne
options.B: Exactly equal per tonne
options.C: Lower per tonne, in view of the economies of full-rake movement
options.D: Applicable only to trains carrying passengers

e: Trainload (rake-load) rates are lower per tonne than wagonload rates for the same commodity and distance, because full-rake movement gives economies of scale in operation and handling.

q: Light and bulky consignments, which occupy space disproportionate to their actual weight, are charged for carriage:

options.A: Only on their actual weight in all cases
options.B: At double the normal freight in all cases
options.C: Only when booked at railway risk
options.D: On the basis of measurement weight, computed from the dimensions of the packages at the prescribed conversion

e: Light and bulky consignments occupying space disproportionate to their weight are charged on measurement weight, computed from the dimensions of the packages at the prescribed conversion, instead of actual weight.

q: An Over Dimensional Consignment (ODC), which infringes the standard moving dimensions, is accepted for carriage:

options.A: Only with prior sanction and subject to special conditions and charges
options.B: Freely, like any ordinary consignment
options.C: Only in wagons owned by the consignor
options.D: Only by passenger-carrying trains

e: An Over Dimensional Consignment infringing the standard moving dimensions is accepted for carriage only with prior sanction and subject to special conditions and charges, as it needs special clearance and precautions en route.

q: Where heavy consignments are loaded or unloaded with the help of railway cranes, the crane charges are:

options.A: Borne by the Railways in all cases
options.B: Adjusted against the demurrage accrued on the consignment
options.C: Recovered from the consignor or the consignee, as the case may be, in addition to the freight
options.D: Included in the wharfage charges of the station

e: Crane charges for loading or unloading heavy consignments with railway cranes are recovered from the consignor or the consignee, as the case may be, in addition to the freight.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Liberalised Wagon Investment Scheme (LWIS):
1. The investor under the scheme is assured of supply of wagons for his traffic.
2. The investor under the scheme is eligible for a rebate in freight.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: under the Liberalised Wagon Investment Scheme the investor is assured of supply of wagons for his traffic and is eligible for a rebate in freight on the traffic moved in those wagons.

q: 'Stabling charges' on the Railways are levied for:

options.A: Keeping railway wagons in workshops for repair
options.B: Stabling of horses of railway officers at stations
options.C: Parking of road vehicles in the station premises
options.D: Stabling or detention of privately owned wagons or rakes on railway lines/premises beyond the time allowed

e: Stabling charges are levied for stabling or detention of privately owned wagons or rakes on railway lines and premises beyond the time allowed.

q:
Consider the following statements about the e-payment system for freight:
1. It works under a tripartite agreement among the Railways, the bank and the freight customer, under which the freight is debited directly to the customer's bank account.
2. Under it, the freight is first collected in cash at the goods shed and is reimbursed to the Railways by the bank later.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: under e-payment, a tripartite agreement among the Railways, the bank and the freight customer provides for freight to be debited directly to the customer's bank account. Statement 2 is false: no cash is collected at the goods shed under this system.

q: Under a Privilege Ticket Order (PTO), a railway employee (with his family, where admissible) can travel on payment of:

options.A: The full public fare
options.B: One-third of the public fare
options.C: One-half of the public fare
options.D: Only the reservation charge

e: Under a Privilege Ticket Order, a railway employee, with his family where admissible, travels on payment of one-third of the public fare.

q: In connection with season tickets, the abbreviations MST and QST stand for:

options.A: Main Station Ticket and Quota Season Ticket
options.B: Monthly Single Ticket and Quarterly Single Ticket
options.C: Monthly Season Ticket and Quarterly Season Ticket
options.D: Multiple Season Ticket and Quick Season Ticket

e: MST stands for Monthly Season Ticket and QST for Quarterly Season Ticket, the two standard season ticket products issued to regular commuters.

q: The 'Emergency Quota' (commonly called the HO quota) in reserved accommodation refers to:

options.A: Berths/seats earmarked for release to high officials and persons in urgent need, released under the orders of the competent authority
options.B: The quota reserved for season ticket holders
options.C: The quota of wagons allotted for emergency goods traffic
options.D: The quota reserved for railway staff travelling on duty passes

e: The Emergency Quota (HO quota) consists of berths and seats earmarked for release to high officials and persons in urgent need, released under the orders of the competent authority.

q: A quota of lower berths in trains is earmarked for allotment, subject to availability and the conditions prescribed, to:

options.A: Season ticket holders
options.B: Foreign tourists only
options.C: Passengers travelling in groups
options.D: Senior citizens, female passengers and pregnant women

e: A quota of lower berths is earmarked for allotment, subject to availability and the prescribed conditions, to senior citizens, female passengers and pregnant women.

q: Under the Premium Tatkal scheme, the premium charges are:

options.A: Fixed at a flat rate for all trains
options.B: Linked to demand and vary (dynamic pricing) within the prescribed limits
options.C: Exactly equal to the normal Tatkal charges
options.D: Charged only for travel in air-conditioned classes in all cases

e: Under the Premium Tatkal scheme, the premium charges are not flat; they are linked to demand and vary under dynamic pricing within the prescribed limits.

q: A passenger holding a through journey ticket may break his journey at an intermediate station:

options.A: In accordance with the break-journey rules, after getting the ticket endorsed where so required
options.B: Under no circumstances whatsoever
options.C: Only at the destination station named on the ticket
options.D: Only in suburban sections

e: A passenger holding a through journey ticket may break his journey at an intermediate station in accordance with the break-journey rules, after getting the ticket endorsed where the rules so require.

q: Lease charges recovered from private operators for leasing of parcel space in brake/luggage vans (SLR) and parcel vans form part of:

options.A: Sundry other earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Parcel earnings, classified under Other Coaching Earnings
options.D: Capital receipts

e: Lease charges recovered for leasing parcel space in brake/luggage vans (SLR) and parcel vans are classified as parcel earnings under Other Coaching Earnings.

q: 'Earnings per goods train kilometre' are computed as:

options.A: Goods earnings divided by wagon kilometres
options.B: Goods earnings divided by the number of wagons owned
options.C: Goods earnings divided by route kilometres
options.D: Goods earnings divided by goods train kilometres

e: Earnings per goods train kilometre = goods earnings divided by goods train kilometres; it measures the average goods realisation per kilometre run by goods trains.

q: 'Earnings per wagon day' are computed as:

options.A: Goods earnings divided by wagon kilometres
options.B: Goods earnings divided by the total wagon days
options.C: Goods earnings divided by the number of wagons loaded
options.D: Goods earnings divided by goods train kilometres

e: Earnings per wagon day = goods earnings divided by the total wagon days, showing the average daily earning obtained from each wagon of the fleet.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cost per passenger kilometre is worked out by dividing the total cost of coaching services by the passenger kilometres performed.
2. A comparison of the earnings per passenger kilometre with the cost per passenger kilometre indicates whether the coaching services are, on the average, remunerative.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: cost per passenger kilometre is the total cost of coaching services divided by the passenger kilometres performed, and comparing it with earnings per passenger kilometre shows whether coaching services are remunerative on the average.

q: Waiver of demurrage may be considered by the competent authority where the detention of wagons was due to:

options.A: Causes attributable to the Railways themselves, such as late placement of wagons for unloading
options.B: The consignee being a regular customer of the Railways
options.C: The high value of the goods loaded in the wagons
options.D: The consignee having engaged his own labour for unloading

e: Demurrage waiver may be considered where the detention of wagons was due to causes attributable to the Railways themselves, such as late placement of wagons for unloading.

q: Where a consignment is taken delivery of in a damaged or deficient condition, the consignee should, in his own interest:

options.A: Refuse delivery in every case
options.B: Pay additional freight for the damage
options.C: Apply for re-weighment of the consignment only
options.D: Get the condition of the consignment recorded in the delivery book at the time of taking delivery

e: A consignee taking delivery of a damaged or deficient consignment should get its condition recorded in the delivery book at the time of delivery, as this record supports his subsequent claim.

q: The losses on an uneconomic branch line which is retained in operation at the request of a State Government are:

options.A: Borne entirely by the Railways in all cases
options.B: Shared with the State Government at whose request the line is retained
options.C: Recovered from the passengers travelling on the line
options.D: Adjusted against the dividend payable to General Revenues

e: Losses on an uneconomic branch line retained in operation at the request of a State Government are shared with that State Government, instead of being borne entirely by the Railways.

q: The Terminal Management System (TMS) module of FOIS deals with:

options.A: Compilation of pay bills of terminal staff
options.B: Maintenance of terminal buildings
options.C: Transactions at goods terminals, such as booking, delivery and related charges
options.D: Training of goods terminal staff

e: The Terminal Management System (TMS) module of FOIS deals with transactions at goods terminals, such as booking, delivery and related charges.

q: The abbreviation SPTM, used at railway stations, stands for:

options.A: Self Printing Ticket Machine
options.B: Station Parcel Traffic Module
options.C: Single Passenger Ticket Machine
options.D: Special Passenger Train Movement

e: SPTM stands for Self Printing Ticket Machine, the machine at stations on which passengers can print tickets booked online by entering the booking details.

q: Luggage found unbooked with a passenger during the journey is:

options.A: Confiscated by the Railways
options.B: Carried free to the destination
options.C: Detrained at the next station in all cases
options.D: Charged at the prescribed luggage scale of charges, together with any penal charges due under the rules

e: Luggage found unbooked with a passenger during the journey is charged at the prescribed luggage scale of charges, together with any penal charges due under the rules.

q: Yatri Ticket Suvidha Kendra (YTSK) licensees are:

options.A: Railway employees posted at stations for ticket issue
options.B: Authorised agents licensed to issue reserved and unreserved tickets from counters outside railway premises
options.C: Contractors engaged for catering services at stations
options.D: Agents authorised for booking of goods traffic only

e: YTSK (Yatri Ticket Suvidha Kendra) licensees are authorised agents licensed to issue reserved and unreserved tickets from counters located outside railway premises.

q: The 'average load of wagons at loading' is computed as:

options.A: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by loaded wagon kilometres
options.B: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by total wagon kilometres
options.C: Total tonnes loaded divided by the number of wagons loaded
options.D: Tonnes carried divided by the number of goods trains

e: Average load of wagons at loading = total tonnes loaded divided by the number of wagons loaded; it shows the average payload put into each wagon at the time of loading.
